question.problem: Claire has sectioned off a triangular area of her garden whose base is $7$ feet and height is $5$ feet to plant some flowers. What is the area of the flowerbed?
question.worked_solution:
Let's sketch the flowerbed based on the description.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14199152/assets/b409d299208280d3be7e33be8e74c3d894fa9f3ad7e5605e4b551b6b0434302a.png)

The height and base of the triangle are

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{base} & =7, \\ \text{height} & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle can be found by the following formula:

$$
\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}\times \text{base}\times \text{height}
$$

Substituting the values of the base and height, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area} & =\frac{1}{2}\times 7\times 5 \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\times 35 \\  & =17.5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's find the units. Since base and height are measured in feet, the area is measured in square feet. Hence,

$$
\text{Area}=17.5\,{\text{ft}}^{2}.
$$
